papers.title: Randomized Matrix-free Trace and Log-Determinant Estimators
papers.abstract: We present randomized algorithms for estimating the trace and deter- minant of Hermitian positive semi-definite matrices. The algorithms are based on subspace iteration, and access the matrix only through matrix vector products. We analyse the error due to randomization, for starting guesses whose elements are Gaussian or Rademacher random variables. The analysis is cleanly separated into a structural (deterministic) part followed by a probabilistic part. Our absolute bounds for the expectation and concentration of the estimators are non-asymptotic and informative even for matrices of low dimension. For the trace estimators, we also present asymptotic bounds on the number of samples (columns of the starting guess) required to achieve a user-specified relative error. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the estimators and the tightness of the bounds on low-dimensional matrices; and on a challenging application in uncertainty quantification arising from Bayesian optimal experimental design.

summary_en.motivation: To develop efficient randomized algorithms for trace and determinant estimation of large matrices accessed only via matrix-vector products.
summary_en.method: Subspace iteration with Gaussian or Rademacher starting guesses.
summary_en.result: Non-asymptotic error bounds and concentration results with numerical validation.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on low-dimensional matrices and a Bayesian optimal experimental design UQ problem.
